title: Enterprise Finance Applications and Payments Platform Landscape

scope.description: Vendors and substitutes that shape Booking Holdings' build-vs-buy, convergence and sourcing decisions for its finance core, subledger, close and planning, and payments-to-ledger. Booking Holdings is a buyer and partner of these firms, not their competitor; the landscape shows which platforms compete for the architecture's slots and what leverage each brings.
scope.inclusionLogic: Included: ERP and finance-suite vendors that could host the global finance core (SAP, Oracle, Workday); close/reconciliation and consolidation/planning specialists reported in a third-party listing of Booking's finance stack (BlackLine, OneStream); global payment service providers whose settlement data and reporting feed payments-to-ledger (Adyen, Stripe); and in-house build as the main substitute. Excluded: implementation partners and system integrators, tax-content and treasury niche vendors without verifiable public metrics, and Booking's own payment entities.
scope.notes: Figures are company-wide and measure different things (revenue in EUR or USD, processed or payment volume) over different fiscal years (SAP and BlackLine and OneStream calendar 2025; Oracle FY ending 31 May 2026; Workday FY ending 31 January 2026; Adyen H2 2025 half-year; Stripe calendar 2025). They are not comparable and say nothing about Booking's own spend. Stripe is private and self-reports. That Booking uses BlackLine or OneStream is an assumption from an unverified third-party job listing; SAP use at Booking.com is stated in Booking.com job postings. Adyen and Stripe are included as PSP categories; no Booking relationship with either is confirmed by an official source.

players.name: SAP
players.description: ERP leader and incumbent of Booking.com's finance core (SAP on HANA, Simple Finance since 2016, S/4HANA journey with Central Finance since 2019, FI-CA and BRIM in the stack per Booking.com job postings). RISE with SAP and the end of standard ECC maintenance shape the convergence timeline and run-cost.

players.description: Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP and NetSuite are the main alternative finance-core platforms, often found in acquired or smaller brands; relevant to brand convergence decisions and as a benchmark in ERP renewals.

players.name: BlackLine
players.description: Close management, account reconciliation and intercompany specialist. Reported (unverified) in Booking's finance stack; competes with SAP's own close and reconciliation tooling for the close-orchestration slot.

players.name: OneStream
players.description: Unified consolidation, reporting and planning platform. Reported (unverified) in Booking's finance stack; competes with SAP Group Reporting and planning suites. Pending acquisition by Hg affects vendor-risk and roadmap decisions.

players.name: Adyen
players.description: Global payment platform for card-not-present and alternative payment methods with travel and OTA offerings. Represents the PSP category whose settlement reports, fees and dispute data feed payments-to-ledger reconciliation.

players.name: Stripe
players.hq: South San Francisco, California, United States and Dublin, Ireland
players.description: Payments and financial infrastructure platform including billing, revenue recognition and treasury APIs; both a PSP and a reference for API-first finance tooling that challenges ERP-centric subledger designs.

players.name: In-house build (brand-specific finance systems)
players.description: Custom ledgers, settlement engines and reconciliation tools built by individual brands. The main substitute for shared platforms: fast locally, but it duplicates spend, fragments controls and slows convergence. Every convergence decision weighs against it.
